title: LETTER WRITING
notes:
✓ Letter writing → a written form of communication used to share information, ideas, requests, feelings, opinions, or official messages.

◆ MAIN TYPES
✓ Formal letters and informal letters.

✓ Formal letter → written to an organization, authority, institution, employer, or someone you do not know personally.
✓ Informal letter → written to friends, family members, or people you know well.

✓ The tone, structure, vocabulary, and purpose should match the type of letter.

title: FORMAL LETTER
notes:
✓ Formal letter → used for official, professional, academic, or serious purposes.

◆ COMMON PURPOSES
✓ Making a complaint
✓ Requesting information
✓ Applying for a job
✓ Asking for permission
✓ Making an inquiry
✓ Applying for admission
✓ Giving official information
✓ Making a suggestion
✓ Requesting a service

✓ Tone → polite, respectful, clear, objective, and professional.

⚠️ Avoid slang, unnecessary personal details, emojis, and overly casual expressions.

title: FORMAL LETTER STRUCTURE
notes:
✓ A formal letter commonly contains:

◆ 1. Sender's address
◆ 2. Date
◆ 3. Receiver's address
◆ 4. Subject
◆ 5. Salutation
◆ 6. Introduction
◆ 7. Main body
◆ 8. Conclusion
◆ 9. Complimentary close
◆ 10. Signature/name

✓ Basic order → Address → Date → Receiver → Subject → Salutation → Body → Closing → Signature.

title: SENDER'S ADDRESS & DATE
notes:
✓ Sender's address → usually appears at the top of a formal letter.

✓ 15 Bole Road
✓ Addis Ababa

✓ Date → written below the sender's address.

✓ 31 August 2026

◆ COMMON DATE STYLES
✓ 31 August 2026
✓ August 31, 2026

✓ In formal academic writing, write the month in words to avoid confusion.

title: RECEIVER'S ADDRESS
notes:
✓ The receiver's address identifies the person, organization, or institution receiving the letter.

✓ The Human Resources Manager
✓ ABC Company
✓ Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

✓ If the person's name is unknown, use their position or department.

◆ EXAMPLES
✓ The Principal
ABC Secondary School
Addis Ababa

✓ The Customer Service Manager
XYZ Company
Addis Ababa

title: SUBJECT LINE
notes:
✓ Subject → briefly states the main purpose of the letter.

✓ Subject: Application for the Position of Computer Technician
✓ Subject: Complaint About Poor Internet Service
✓ Subject: Request for School Admission

✓ A good subject is short, specific, and directly related to the purpose.

⚠️ Do not write the entire letter in the subject line.

title: FORMAL SALUTATION
notes:
✓ If the receiver's name is known:
✓ Dear Mr. Ahmed,
✓ Dear Ms. Hana,
✓ Dear Dr. Bekele,

✓ If the name is unknown:
✓ Dear Sir/Madam,

✓ Use a comma after the salutation in common modern formats.

⚠️ Avoid casual greetings such as:
❌ Hi bro,
❌ Hello friend,
❌ Hey!

title: FORMAL LETTER INTRODUCTION
notes:
✓ The opening paragraph should immediately state the reason for writing.

✓ I am writing to apply for the position of...
✓ I am writing to express my concern about...
✓ I am writing to request information about...
✓ I am writing to complain about...
✓ I am writing in response to...
✓ I would like to inquire about...

✓ Avoid unnecessarily long introductions. State the purpose clearly.

title: FORMAL LETTER BODY
notes:
✓ The body contains the important details supporting the purpose of the letter.

◆ ORGANIZATION
✓ Paragraph 1 → purpose/background.
✓ Paragraph 2 → important details, facts, or explanation.
✓ Paragraph 3 → requested action, solution, or expected response.

✓ Use short, organized paragraphs rather than one large block of text.

✓ Each paragraph should have one clear purpose.

title: FORMAL REQUESTS
notes:
✓ Useful expressions for polite requests:

✓ I would be grateful if you could...
✓ I would appreciate it if you could...
✓ I kindly request that you...
✓ Could you please provide...?
✓ I would like to request...
✓ I am writing to ask for...
✓ I would appreciate your assistance with...

⚠️ Avoid overly direct forms in formal writing.

❌ Give me the information.
✓ I would appreciate it if you could provide the information.

title: FORMAL COMPLAINT LETTER
notes:
✓ Complaint letter → used to report a problem and request an appropriate solution.

◆ STRUCTURE
✓ 1. State the reason for writing.
✓ 2. Explain the problem clearly.
✓ 3. Give relevant dates/details.
✓ 4. Explain the effect of the problem.
✓ 5. Request a reasonable solution.
✓ 6. End politely.

✓ I am writing to complain about...
✓ Unfortunately, I have experienced...
✓ This has caused considerable inconvenience...
✓ I would appreciate it if this matter could be resolved promptly.

✓ Be firm but respectful.

title: JOB APPLICATION LETTER
notes:
✓ A job application letter introduces the applicant and explains why they are suitable for a position.

◆ INCLUDE
✓ Position being applied for
✓ Relevant education
✓ Skills and experience
✓ Qualifications
✓ Interest in the organization
✓ Availability/interview request

✓ I am writing to apply for the position of...
✓ I believe my skills and qualifications make me a suitable candidate for this position.
✓ I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my application in an interview.

⚠️ Keep claims truthful, specific, and relevant to the position.

title: LETTER OF INQUIRY
notes:
✓ Inquiry letter → requests information about a product, service, course, job, institution, or opportunity.

✓ I am writing to inquire about...
✓ I would like to know whether...
✓ Could you please provide information about...?
✓ I would appreciate further information regarding...

✓ Clearly state exactly what information you need.

title: LETTER OF SUGGESTION
notes:
✓ Suggestion letter → proposes an improvement or solution.

◆ STRUCTURE
✓ Identify the issue.
✓ Explain why improvement is needed.
✓ Present your suggestion.
✓ Explain its benefits.
✓ Request consideration.

✓ I would like to suggest that...
✓ One possible solution would be to...
✓ This could help to...
✓ I believe this would improve...

title: FORMAL CONCLUSION
notes:
✓ The conclusion should summarize the expected action or politely indicate that a response is appreciated.

✓ I look forward to hearing from you.
✓ I look forward to your response.
✓ Thank you for your time and consideration.
✓ I would appreciate your prompt attention to this matter.
✓ Please do not hesitate to contact me if further information is required.

✓ Keep the ending polite and relevant.

title: FORMAL CLOSING
notes:
✓ Common formal closings:

✓ Yours faithfully, → commonly used when the recipient's name is unknown.

✓ Yours sincerely, → commonly used when the recipient's name is known.

✓ Kind regards, → professional and less traditional.

✓ Traditional exam rule:
Dear Sir/Madam → Yours faithfully.
Dear Mr./Ms. + name → Yours sincerely.

title: INFORMAL LETTER
notes:
✓ Informal letter → written to someone you know personally, such as a friend, relative, or close acquaintance.

◆ COMMON PURPOSES
✓ Sharing news
✓ Giving advice
✓ Inviting someone
✓ Describing an experience
✓ Congratulating someone
✓ Thanking someone
✓ Apologizing
✓ Giving personal information

✓ Tone → friendly, natural, personal, and conversational.

title: INFORMAL LETTER STRUCTURE
notes:
✓ A typical informal letter contains:

◆ 1. Sender's address
◆ 2. Date
◆ 3. Greeting
◆ 4. Opening/personal introduction
◆ 5. Main body
◆ 6. Closing paragraph
◆ 7. Friendly sign-off

✓ Basic order → Address → Date → Greeting → Introduction → Body → Closing → Sign-off.

title: INFORMAL GREETINGS
notes:
✓ Common informal greetings:

✓ Dear John,
✓ Dear Hana,
✓ Hi John,
✓ Hi Sara,

✓ The greeting should match the relationship with the recipient.

✓ Informal letters can use more personal language than formal letters.

✓ How are you?
✓ I hope you're doing well.
✓ It was great to hear from you.

title: INFORMAL LETTER LANGUAGE
notes:
✓ Informal letters can use contractions and conversational expressions.

✓ I'm → I am
✓ we're → we are
✓ don't → do not
✓ can't → cannot
✓ I'll → I will

✓ Thanks for your letter.
✓ It was great to hear from you.
✓ I'm really happy about the news.
✓ Write back soon.

⚠️ Informal does not mean careless. Grammar, spelling, and punctuation still matter.

title: INFORMAL LETTER PURPOSES
notes:
✓ Invitation → I'd love you to come to...

✓ Congratulations → Congratulations on your success!

✓ Thanks → Thanks so much for...

✓ Advice → If I were you, I would...

✓ Apology → I'm really sorry about...

✓ Experience → Last weekend, I went to...

✓ News → I've got some exciting news...

✓ Match the vocabulary and tone with the purpose of the letter.

title: INFORMAL CLOSINGS
notes:
✓ Common informal sign-offs:

✓ Best wishes,
✓ All the best,
✓ Take care,
✓ See you soon,
✓ Love,
✓ Lots of love,

✓ Use the closing according to your relationship with the recipient.

⚠️ Avoid very intimate closings when writing to someone who is only a casual acquaintance.

title: FORMAL VS INFORMAL
notes:
◆ FORMAL
✓ Professional/official purpose.
✓ Polite and objective tone.
✓ More formal vocabulary.
✓ Avoid slang.
✓ Clear paragraphs.
✓ Often includes subject line.
✓ Yours faithfully/sincerely.

◆ INFORMAL
✓ Personal purpose.
✓ Friendly tone.
✓ Conversational vocabulary.
✓ Contractions are acceptable.
✓ Personal feelings and experiences.
✓ Friendly sign-off.

✓ The biggest difference → audience + purpose + tone.

title: FORMAL VOCABULARY UPGRADE
notes:
❌ I want → ✓ I would like to request...
❌ Give me → ✓ Could you please provide...?
❌ Tell me → ✓ I would appreciate information about...
❌ I don't like → ✓ I am dissatisfied with...
❌ Fix this → ✓ I kindly request that this issue be resolved.
❌ I need help → ✓ I would appreciate your assistance.
❌ Sorry → ✓ I sincerely apologize.

✓ Formal writing uses polite, precise, and professional expressions rather than direct or emotional language.

title: LINKING EXPRESSIONS
notes:
✓ Use linking words to organize ideas.

◆ Addition → furthermore, moreover, in addition, also

◆ Result → therefore, consequently, as a result

◆ Reason → because, since, due to, as

◆ Contrast → however, although, whereas, nevertheless

◆ Example → for example, for instance

◆ Conclusion → therefore, in conclusion, finally

✓ Good linking expressions make a letter clearer and more logical.

title: COMMON LETTER-WRITING ERRORS
notes:
❌ Dear Sir/Madam, ... Yours sincerely,
✓ Dear Sir/Madam, ... Yours faithfully,

❌ Dear Mr. Ahmed, ... Yours faithfully,
✓ Dear Mr. Ahmed, ... Yours sincerely,

❌ I am writing this letter because I want to tell you many things...
✓ I am writing to request information about...

❌ Give me a response quickly.
✓ I would appreciate your prompt response.

❌ One huge paragraph.
✓ Divide ideas into clear paragraphs.

❌ Excessive slang in a formal letter.
✓ Use professional language.

❌ Repeating the same point.
✓ Keep the message focused and concise.
